newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's sugar output falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's sugar output falls sharply.

text.p: Pakistan's sugar production for fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) fell 42.87 percent to 388,272 tonnes by December 15 compared to 679,635 tonnes in the year-ago period, Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said on Monday.

The Association gave no reason for the fall, but one dealer attributed it to the late start of sugarcane crushing season in November instead of October to enable the mills to get more sugar from sugarcane.
Pakistan is likely to produce 2.65 million tonnes in 1996/97 compared to 2.47 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 3.0 million tonnes in 1994/95.
On reports of the shortfall, the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan bought 50,000 tonnes of sugar last week from neighbouring India for shipment by January 11, the dealer said.
